statement: Whenever `minimum_time(n, relations, time)` returns a result `r`, `r` equals the maximum weight over all directed paths. A directed path is a sequence `(v_0, ..., v_k)` with `k >= 0`, each `v_i` in `{1,...,n}`, such that for every `i` with `0 <= i < k` the pair `[v_i, v_{i+1}]` occurs in `relations` (i.e., equals `relations[j]` for some `j`). Its weight is `sum_{i=0}^k time[v_i - 1]`. The maximum is well-defined because there is at least one directed path (the one-course path `(c)` for any `c`) and the graph is finite and acyclic.
preconditions: `n` is an integer with `1 <= n <= 50000`; `len(time) = n`; for every `i` with `0 <= i < n`, `1 <= time[i] <= 10000`; every entry of `relations` is a pair `[a,b]` with `1 <= a,b <= n`, `a != b`; all such pairs are distinct; `len(relations) <= min(n*(n-1)/2, 50000)`; and the directed graph on vertices `1..n` with edges given by `relations` is acyclic.

statement: The call `minimum_time(n, relations, time)` returns a result `r` (it does not fail).
preconditions: `n` is an integer with `1 <= n <= 50000`; `len(time) = n`; for every `i` with `0 <= i < n`, `1 <= time[i] <= 10000`; every entry of `relations` is a pair `[a,b]` with `1 <= a,b <= n`, `a != b`; all such pairs are distinct; `len(relations) <= min(n*(n-1)/2, 50000)`; and the directed graph on vertices `1..n` with edges given by `relations` is acyclic.

statement: Whenever `minimum_time(n, relations, time)` returns a result `r`, for every course `c` with `1 <= c <= n`, `r >= time[c-1]`. Equivalently, `r >= max_{0 <= i < n} time[i]`.
preconditions: `n` is an integer with `1 <= n <= 50000`; `len(time) = n`; for every `i` with `0 <= i < n`, `1 <= time[i] <= 10000`; every entry of `relations` is a pair `[a,b]` with `1 <= a,b <= n`, `a != b`; all such pairs are distinct; `len(relations) <= min(n*(n-1)/2, 50000)`; and the directed graph on vertices `1..n` with edges given by `relations` is acyclic.

statement: Whenever `minimum_time(n, relations, time)` returns a result `r`, `r <= sum_{i=0}^{n-1} time[i]`.
preconditions: `n` is an integer with `1 <= n <= 50000`; `len(time) = n`; for every `i` with `0 <= i < n`, `1 <= time[i] <= 10000`; every entry of `relations` is a pair `[a,b]` with `1 <= a,b <= n`, `a != b`; all such pairs are distinct; `len(relations) <= min(n*(n-1)/2, 50000)`; and the directed graph on vertices `1..n` with edges given by `relations` is acyclic.

statement: Whenever `minimum_time(n, relations, time)` returns a result `r`, there exists a directed path `P = (v_0,...,v_k)` with `k >= 0`, each `v_i` in `1..n`, and each consecutive pair occurring in `relations`, whose weight `sum_{i=0}^k time[v_i-1]` is exactly `r`.
preconditions: `n` is an integer with `1 <= n <= 50000`; `len(time) = n`; for every `i` with `0 <= i < n`, `1 <= time[i] <= 10000`; every entry of `relations` is a pair `[a,b]` with `1 <= a,b <= n`, `a != b`; all such pairs are distinct; `len(relations) <= min(n*(n-1)/2, 50000)`; and the directed graph on vertices `1..n` with edges given by `relations` is acyclic.

statement: Whenever `minimum_time(n, relations, time)` returns a result `r`, for every pair `[u,v]` that occurs in `relations`, `r >= time[u-1] + time[v-1]`.
preconditions: `n` is an integer with `1 <= n <= 50000`; `len(time) = n`; for every `i` with `0 <= i < n`, `1 <= time[i] <= 10000`; every entry of `relations` is a pair `[a,b]` with `1 <= a,b <= n`, `a != b`; all such pairs are distinct; `len(relations) <= min(n*(n-1)/2, 50000)`; and the directed graph on vertices `1..n` with edges given by `relations` is acyclic.

statement: For each course `c` with `1 <= c <= n`, let `D(c)` be the maximum weight of a directed path ending at `c` (the one-course path `(c)` is allowed). Whenever `minimum_time(n, relations, time)` returns a result `r`, (i) `r = max_{1 <= c <= n} D(c)`, and (ii) for every course `c`, `D(c) = time[c-1] + max(0, max{D(u) : [u,c] occurs in relations})`, where the maximum over an empty set of predecessors is defined to be `0`.
preconditions: `n` is an integer with `1 <= n <= 50000`; `len(time) = n`; for every `i` with `0 <= i < n`, `1 <= time[i] <= 10000`; every entry of `relations` is a pair `[a,b]` with `1 <= a,b <= n`, `a != b`; all such pairs are distinct; `len(relations) <= min(n*(n-1)/2, 50000)`; and the directed graph on vertices `1..n` with edges given by `relations` is acyclic.

statement: Whenever `minimum_time(n, relations, time)` returns a result `r`, `r = max_{0 <= i < n} time[i]`.
preconditions: `n` is an integer with `1 <= n <= 50000`; `len(time) = n`; for every `i` with `0 <= i < n`, `1 <= time[i] <= 10000`; `len(relations) = 0`; all entries of `relations` are distinct pairs; and the directed graph on vertices `1..n` with edges given by `relations` is acyclic.

statement: Whenever `minimum_time(n, relations, time)` returns a result `r`, `r = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} time[i]`.
preconditions: `n` is an integer with `1 <= n <= 50000`; `len(time) = n`; for every `i` with `0 <= i < n`, `1 <= time[i] <= 10000`; every entry of `relations` is a pair `[a,b]` with `1 <= a,b <= n`, `a != b`; all such pairs are distinct; `len(relations) <= min(n*(n-1)/2, 50000)`; the directed graph on vertices `1..n` with edges given by `relations` is acyclic; and there exists a directed path that contains every course `1..n` exactly once (a Hamiltonian directed path).

statement: If `minimum_time(n, relations, time1)` returns `r1` and `minimum_time(n, relations, time2)` returns `r2`, then `r1 >= r2`.
preconditions: Let `time1` and `time2` be two arrays such that `(n, relations, time1)` and `(n, relations, time2)` both satisfy the problem constraints, and `time1[i] >= time2[i]` for every `0 <= i < n`.

statement: If `minimum_time(n, relations, time)` returns `r` and `minimum_time(n, relations', time)` returns `r'`, then `r = r'`.
preconditions: `n` is an integer with `1 <= n <= 50000`; `time` has length `n` with entries in `1..10000`; `relations` satisfies the problem constraints; and `relations'` is a permutation of the list `relations` (same length and same multiset of pairs) such that `(n, relations', time)` also satisfies the problem constraints.

statement: If `minimum_time(n, relations, time)` returns `r` and `minimum_time(n, relations', time)` returns `r'`, then `r' >= r`.
preconditions: `n` is an integer with `1 <= n <= 50000`; `time` has length `n` with entries in `1..10000`; `relations` and `relations'` are two prerequisite lists for the same `n` and `time`, both satisfying the problem constraints, and every pair occurring in `relations` also occurs in `relations'`.

statement: Whenever `minimum_time(n, relations, time)` returns a result `r`, `r = max( max_{0 <= i < n} time[i], time[u-1] + time[v-1] )`.
preconditions: The input satisfies the problem constraints, `n > 2`, `len(relations) = 1`, and the unique relation is `[u,v]`.
